articles.title: Tetris Responds After Trump Administration Launches 'Build the Wall' Clone Game
articles.summary: Official Tetris pages have responded after the Trump administration launched a clone video game called 'Build the Wall.'. The Tetris Company joined the backlash after Donald Trump's White House published its Arcade.Gov website today.
body: A description for the game follows: "Protect the border from the coming horde." It's a message that Tetris wants absolutely nothing to do with.

"At Tetris we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them," it said. "To our fans everywhere: we love you, we see you, and we're grateful to have you in our community."

Tetris continued, confirming that it had nothing to do with the Trump administration's Build the Wall game. It also added, "We take copyright infringement very seriously." The Tetris Company does not seem to have taken any sort of legal action against the arcade page yet.

The White House launched its website yesterday. It contains five games, including titles asking players to "border patrol along the Rio Grande" and "fill your kids' Trump accounts." It also warned that more games are coming soon.

articles.title: Hideki Kamiya Isn't Fussed About the Physical vs. Digital Debate – He Just Wants Games to Be Preserved for Future Generations
articles.summary: Hideki Kamiya, creator of Bayonetta and director of Resident Evil 2, said he isn’t too fussed about physical vs digital games; instead, he’s more concerned with preserving games for players to enjoy in the future. Hideki Kamiya is behind some of the biggest franchises in gaming history.
body: In his usual candid manner, Kamiya admitted he doesn’t actually buy physical games at all anymore, as told in a September 2 interview with Video Games Chronicle.
"I don’t buy a single physical game these days – every single game I buy is 100% digital, so I look at that decision and think, 'Yeah, I guess this is where things were heading,'" he told the outlet.

He went on to say that the disc vs digital debate isn’t really relevant for him; instead, he hopes publishers make efforts to preserve their games for future generations of players, no matter what form that might take.

"That’s the big thing for me, is whether or not the IP holders are going to take responsibility for ensuring that all of these games will continue to be available to future generations in order for them to be played. Whether that’s physically or digitally is less important to me, just so long as these games will be available to people in the future," he continued.

articles.title: Steam Users Can Play This Chaotic Among Us-like for Free Until Sept. 7
articles.summary: First Class Trouble is free to play on Steam this weekend, letting you team up with friends, uncover traitors, and cause chaos aboard a space cruise.
body: Few things are better than getting a group of friends together online for some multiplayer chaos, and we're in a golden age for party gaming.

Among Us has basically reached legend status at this point. Then you've got games like Peak and REPO, which are guaranteed to turn a night of gaming with friends into a good time — assuming everyone survives and isn't sabotaging the crew. And right now, Meccha Chameleon is the latest hot indie game giving players another excuse to get a group together and cause some chaos.

But there are so many party games out there beyond the ones that manage to dominate Steam charts and social media feeds. Some fly a little under the radar, despite offering exactly the kind of ridiculous multiplayer fun that makes these games so easy to love. One of them is about to give you a particularly good excuse to round up your friends, because it's going free-to-play for the entire weekend.

That game is First Class Trouble, an indie party game from Invisible Walls that mixes cooperation, deception, and plenty of opportunities for things to go horribly wrong. And if you're looking for something new to play with friends this weekend, it's free to try on Steam right now.

articles.title: How to Watch Free Movies and TV Shows on Your PS5
articles.summary: Sony recently announced an entirely new feature for PS5 users: free live TV. In short, any PS5 owner with a PlayStation account now has access to a range of ad-supported live TV channels directly through their console, no extra charge.
body: Still, the new “Live TV on PS5” feature isn’t the only way you can watch movies and TV for free. Below, I’ve broken down how to access the new app, as well as what other (potentially better) free media options you have on your console.

To access the new live TV channels, you’ll need a PlayStation 5 and a PlayStation account. Right now, the new Live TV feature is only available in the U.S., with plans to expand into Canada in the near future.

While PlayStation technically says the service doesn't require a subscription, this PlayStation account will be used to link to a Sony Core Pictures account, which predates this new feature. It’s what you’d use to buy or rent movies and series through your PlayStation, kind of similar to Prime Video, and is also available as a separate streaming subscription.

The user interface replicates the cable style of live TV, giving you an opportunity to see upcoming schedules for each available channel. As with most modern streaming interfaces, you’ll also get personalized and themed recommendations.

articles.title: Rockstar Censors GTA 6 Extended Look Trailer for China
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has published a heavily censored version of the Grand Theft Auto 6 extended look reveal for China. As shared by @videotech on X/Twitter, the studio behind the game that is convincing publishers to steer clear of November published its 27-minute gameplay reveal on Chinese social media…
body: Considering this is a Grand Theft Auto game, there's quite a bit you can't see. Footage of protagonists Jason and Lucia at a nightclub, for example, basically turns the screen into a giant purple blur. A later scene blurs out Jason's hand when he's smoking, while brief shots of the beach censor some of the crowd. While most corpses seem unblurred, footage showing close-ups of bloodied dead bodies has also been completely censored.

It's a very different look at GTA 6, but the video wasn't originally the blurry mess we see here. As spotted by GTAForums user BDF, this reportedly isn't the same video Rockstar originally uploaded following GTA 6: Extended Look's Netflix premiere.
The first upload supposedly didn't have the same censoring it does now. Rockstar is said to have altered the video around August 31. The reasoning behind the delayed adjustments is unclear.

articles.title: All match overrides and console locations in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4
articles.summary: Match overrides change the way you play Fortnite in Chapter 7 Season 4. Here are all the match overrides and where to find override consoles.
body: Match overrides allow you to change how Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 is played, but only if you interact with the override console first.

Luckily, override consoles will spawn in the same locations every game and they can be activated every game. However, only one override console will be activatable at a time, and it'll be activatable at a random time during the match. More override consoles can activate later on in a game, but the number will vary.

If you're the first person to interact with a console, you can choose between three match overrides, each of which will adjust the rules in your Fortnite game. These overrides can increase your sprint speed, give you more XP, make your pickaxes deal more damage, and much more. Some match overrides might also only affect your squad, rather than the entire lobby.
Below we've listed where you can find every override console in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 and all the match overrides.

articles.title: Game Director Finally Addresses His Rumored Foot Fetish–Wait, Not Kojima, The Other One
articles.summary: A prolific Japanese game developer has finally addressed all that weird foot imagery in his video games. What? No, I'm not talking about Hideo Kojima (he's busy hanging out with The Backrooms director right now, anyway).
body: “It's not necessarily something I’m consistently aware of--maybe it’s something subconscious coming through,” Miyazaki told The Guardian in response to a question about all the hand imagery in his upcoming action-RPG, The Duskbloods. "Take a look online and there’s a rumor that I have a bit of a thing for feet, but I’m not honestly sure where this comes from."

Though Miyazaki says he's not sure where the idea that he has a "thing for feet" comes from, it's something fans of his games have noticed for years. Whether we're talking The Maiden in Black from Demons' Souls or Priscilla (or Gwunevere, or Sister Friede, or Maneater Mildred) from Dark Souls, it's hard to ignore how many barefoot women are roaming Miyazaki's fictional worlds. Elden Ring's Malenia is rocking bare feet, too, although hers are metal prosthetics. The game's beaches even differentiate between barefoot players and those who are wearing footwear.
So what's with all the shoeless women in Souls games? According to Miyazaki, it's about depicting the human experience. Or something.
"I feel like I’m trying to depict some side of human nature or the human existence that is difficult to describe,” he elaborated.

articles.summary: Happy weekend! As we kick off a new month and prepare for the fall, streamers have packed slates when it comes to their TV programming. This week, some of the new releases include Guy Ritchie's latest action series and an offbeat sports-comedy led by Glen Powell.
body: The Gentlemen is back for a second season, continuing the story of Eddie Horniman (Theo James) and his growing illegal cannabis empire. Chad Powers is also back for a second season, bringing more of Glen Powell’s shenanigans in disguise, a genre he's made his own over the past couple of years. The second season finds him struggling to keep up his fake identity as a football talent with the use of prosthetics and a cheap wig.

Guy Ritchie is back with the second season of The Gentlemen, based on his 2019 movie of the same name. It continues the story of a British soldier who unexpectedly inherits his father’s massive estate, becoming the Duke of Halstead. He then learns that the estate houses a huge illegal cannabis operation.

The Gentlemen is visually stunning, filled with luxurious sets, gorgeous costumes, and the high-energy chase scenes and chaotic shootouts Ritchie does so well. But the director also has too many close-up shots of cast members speaking directly at the camera that fail to take advantage of all the sumptuous scenery.

articles.title: Two Nintendo Directs Announced For Next Week, Including A Zelda Presentation
articles.summary: Not one, but two Nintendo Directs are coming next week. Nintendo has confirmed that a Legend of Zelda Direct will be held on September 8 at 7 AM PT / 10 AM ET, and it'll be followed by a Nintendo Direct on September 9 at the same times.
body: Rumors of a Nintendo Direct began picking up earlier this week after Ubisoft announced that a new look at Just Dance: Decades of Hits was on the way. It's worth noting that the publisher announced it for September 10, but given how often Just Dance games appear in Nintendo broadcasts, it was assumed this would be the date of a Nintendo Direct. With Nintendo hosting a September Nintendo Direct almost every year for the past decade--with 2024 being an exception--it looked like it was only a matter of time before the broadcast was officially announced.

As for what you can expect, Nintendo is keeping its lips zipped for now. Last year's September Direct was focused on several first-party games, smaller third-party titles, and the surprise reveal of a new Virtual Boy headset designed for Switch consoles, so we're guessing that it'll be more of the same for 2026. Following the release of the Switch 2 in 2025 and a steady stream of first-party games, 2026 has been slower by comparison, so here's hoping we get to see what new experiences Nintendo is working on. Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is out later this month, so we'll probably get a new trailer for the turn-based tactics game.

articles.summary: A large portion of the internet pointed their virtual fingers at Humankind 2's new trailer and shouted 'AI slop!' body: The turn-based strategy game's reveal trailer "combined live-action filmmaking, practical sets, custom-made props, costumes, visual effects, and CGI to recreate thousands of years of history in just a few seconds," the studio told Eurogamer over email. "To create the behind-the-scenes trailer, Amplitude Studios once again partnered with BETC, the creative agency behind several previous Humankind trailers."

A new behind-the-scenes video now shows that process off and, yep, those are real humans alright. "Made by humankind" sort of erases the hard work done by all those chickens, a pig, that snake, three horses and a horde of rats, though.

Humankind 2, the actual game, is promising all the historical manipulation and turn-based tinkering you would expect after the first game. This time around, the sequel's adding in an updated UI, new progression systems and improved visuals. We should hear more about what's changing soon as Humankind 2 is set to launch in 2027.

articles.title: Steam Has Generated $15 Billion In Revenue So Far In 2026, And New Games Are A Big Part Of It
articles.summary: As the platform that gets the lion's share of PC game sales, Steam naturally makes a lot of money every year from commissions, publishing fees, and more through its storefront. But how much cash has it made so far in 2026?
body: Steam's top releases by gross revenue include AAA games and breakout indie hits, with Forza Horizon 6 leading the charge. The new racing game earned Steam $210.5 million in revenue, while Crimson Desert sales were responsible for $203.3 million, Resident Evil Requiem made just over $200.9 million, and Slay the Spire 2 brought in over $148 million. Rounding out the list is Subnautica 2 at $139.2 million and Meccha Chameleon at $89.8 million.

Looking ahead, Steam's coffers can expect an influx of cash from highly anticipated releases like Phantom Blade Zero, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and Gears of War: E-Day, just to name a few. Valve gets a cut from whatever is sold on Steam, including the lucrative microtransactions and DLC that accompany most games these days. articles.title: Nearly a decade on, legendary director Hideki Kamiya says he's "100% serious" about reviving Xbox's canned Scalebound
articles.summary: Hideki Kamiya was being super serious about resurrecting Scalebound, PlatinumGames' dragon-filled romp that was cancelled by Xbox nearly a decade ago.
body: The famed director has been at the helm of almost too many beloved games - Bayonetta, Resident Evil 2, Devil May Cry, Okami - so it's pretty easy to look back and wonder what could've been with his canned Xbox project. But it seems that thought pops up in Kamiya's head now and then, too.

When asked if he's spoken to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma about reviving the game, in an interview with VGC, Kamiya said no, but he's more than willing to rekindle the professional relationship. "Now's my opportunity to once again say that if they want to do it, let's make it happen!" He also mentioned that a number of PlatinumGames alumni now work at his new development studio Clovers, which is currently making Okami 2, another long-awaited comeback.

"Of course, it's very unfortunate that the project was unable to see the light of day ultimately, and that is something that even now I still very strongly desire to be able to see through if it's all possible, and I'm being 100% serious when I say that," Kamiya continued.

videos.summary: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse will be released on October 15th, 2026 (Thursday), and pre-orders are now being accepted! In 1499, as the bells announcing the end of medieval Paris ring out, the French capital is under attack by a horde of monsters that have suddenly appeared.
body: Trevor Belmont, the hero who killed Dracula and wields the sacred whip "Vampire Killer," and his daughter Rose Belmont, begin exploring the city and hunting down the monsters to uncover the source of this calamity. Rose soon finds herself entangled in a dark conspiracy lurking behind it all. Can she save Paris?

Tune in to KONAMI PRESS START, for a showcase featuring the latest news and updates on Konami's upcoming projects and current available titles, including SILENT HILL: Townfall, Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse, and Rev. NOiR.
